proofs.full_local_argument: Local clarification of the short source argument for the selected real specialization, and explicit repetition schedule; this paragraph is not quoted source text. If M=M^T, then u^TMv-v^TMu=u^T(M-M^T)v=0 identically. Otherwise choose a nonzero row a^T of A=M-M^T. Since v has independent standard normal coordinates, a^Tv is a real normal variable with variance ||a||_2^2>0, so Pr(a^Tv=0)=0. In particular Pr(Av!=0)>=1/2. Conditional on any v with t=Av!=0, independence gives u^Tt a normal distribution with variance ||t||_2^2>0; consequently Pr(u^Tt!=0 | v)=1, and in particular it is at least 1/2. Integrating this conditional probability yields detection probability at least 1/4, the conservative bound recorded by the source. With independent trials, the chance all r trials miss is at most (3/4)^r. For r=ceil(log(1/delta)/log(4/3)), this is at most delta. There are exactly two right-matvec calls per trial before optional early rejection. No stronger probability-one theorem is extracted here.
proofs.locator: Section 3.3, PDF pp16–17; complete proof on p17
map: For symmetric M, the tested scalar identity always holds.
Set A=M-M^T. For nonsymmetric M, A is nonzero and equality is equivalent to u^TAv=0.

The source writes t_i=sum_j A_ij v_j. A nonzero t_i occurs with probability at least 1/2; conditioning on such a coordinate, a further independent u_i detects a nonzero scalar with probability at least 1/2. Its stated detection bound is therefore at least 1/4.
Repeat independently to amplify the success probability.

assumptions: Exact real arithmetic, exact equality comparisons and ideal independent Gaussian sampling.
The input M is fixed independently of the tester's randomness.
Reject upon any failed equality; accept only if every trial passes.
statement.conclusion: At most 2r right-matvec queries suffice. Each trial detects nonsymmetry with probability at least 1/4, so false acceptance is at most (3/4)^r<=delta. Thus query cost is O(1+log(1/delta)), or O(log(1/delta)) for 0<delta<=1/2, with constants independent of n and M. This is the real specialization of Theorem 4; the explicit integer schedule is a local elaboration of its repetition argument.
statement.objects_and_definitions: For a fixed M in R^{n x n}, symmetry means M=M^T. A right query v in R^n returns the exact vector Mv. In each independent trial draw u,v independently from N(0,I_n), query Mu and Mv, and compare u^T Mv with v^T Mu.
statement.parameter_domains: n>=1 integer; 0<delta<1. Use r=ceil(log(1/delta)/log(4/3)) independent trials.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every integer n>=1, every fixed real M and every delta in (0,1), probability is over all independently sampled trial vectors. Symmetric inputs are accepted with probability 1; nonsymmetric inputs are rejected with probability at least 1-delta.

use_restrictions: No approximate-symmetry, finite-precision, Hermitian-testing or lower-bound claim.
